thread:
olivia: Proposal: add a console 'route lock' to pin a route to a specific API version (v1/v2) for a TTL. Use-case: customers hit regressions during v2 rollouts and need a quick safety button. Thoughts? :railway_track:
raj: 👍 Strong +1. Two constraints: billing must charge by executed version and quotas must use that version's unitization.
casey: Implementation idea: router sets header X-Redwood-Effective-Version on forwarded requests. Billing and quota services read it. Also write a span tag for robustness.
morgan: UX: modal with TTL (1h/24h/7d), reason field, and a preview that estimates cost & latency delta based on recent traffic. Show a big warning when locking to deprecated versions.
olivia: Opt for default soft lock (99% to locked version, 1% probes) and an admin-only hard lock. Soft lets us detect regressions without full rollback.
raj: Caching: maintain lock table in router cache with invalidation on change. Need to guard against invalidation storms. Backoff + batching updates.
casey: Telemetry: emit lock.created, lock.toggled, lock.expired. Also start a 1k-request trace sampling window after lock to detect regressions early.
morgan: Rollout UX: console suggests lock if p99 errors increase >5% post-rollout and shows a click-to-lock suggestion (requires confirm).
ops-bot: Created ticket RW-14299: route-lock + effective-version header. Deploy window request: routing-service v3 tomorrow 03:00 UTC.
olivia: Next steps: raj + casey prototype header + cache; morgan mock modal; ops watch deploy. Sync tomorrow 09:00 PT. :calendar:
